title: Felwine Sarr, writer: 'African Nations' budgets could be directed toward dignity'
subhead: In a new essay, the Senegalese writer explores what might foster the emergence of African societies more focused on individual dignity. In an interview with Le Monde, he argues that public policies must be rethought and redefined around local philosophies and resources.

French court shuts down establishment hosting paid gang bangs in Paris
subhead: France's highest administrative court upheld the temporary closure of a venue that hosted these sexual activities in mid-July while awaiting a final ruling. The court found that the events at the establishment exposed women to 'serious risks' to their physical and psychological well-being, but it did not ban the practices themselves.

title: Alain Robert, the 'French Spiderman': 'Falling is not an option'
subhead: In an interview with Le Monde, climber Alain Robert reflects on the sensation that drives him to risk his life by scaling the world's tallest skyscrapers without any ropes.

title: Adolf and Rudolf Dassler, the Cain and Abel of sports shoes
subhead: 'Sewn and torn' (6/6). Love stories and friendships can sometimes end badly, even in the world of fashion. United by their passion for sports, the two German brothers grew their shoe factory for more than a decade. Separated by WWII, each went on to create his own brand, Adidas and Puma, through which their fierce rivalry was played out.

title: 'The End of Oak Street': Jurassic Park comes to suburban America
subhead: Blending prehistoric science fiction with a satire of American suburbia, David Robert Mitchell playfully subverts the conventions of Steven Spielberg's blockbuster, delivering a B-movie that is both wild and cleverly twisted.

subhead: According to a working document seen by Le Monde, UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC want to change FIFA's presidency into a rotating, representative and ceremonial role with a 'fixed two-year term,' modeled on the Swiss Confederation.

title: 'We are losing our youth': In northern Morocco, mourning those who drowned off Ceuta
subhead: In Tétouan, families mourn the deaths of many young men who tried to swim to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta at the end of July. According to a Moroccan non-profit organization, over 140 people lost their lives. Despite these tragedies, many still dream of reaching Europe clandestinely.

title: Finland wants to restore its peatlands to help the environment. And to slow Russian tanks.
subhead: The Nordic country has identified 180,000 hectares of wetlands that, if restored, could benefit not only the climate and biodiversity but also national defense. While the military supports the plan, some environmentalists warn against rushing the process.
